articles.title: From 'Just Harriet' to HIV Vaccine Pioneer: A Scientist's Unlikely Journey
articles.summary: In a field where male colleagues were 'Doctor,' Harriet Robinson was just 'Harriet.' But that didn't stop her from co-founding a biotech company at 60 to develop an HIV vaccine. Her path—from Russian guide to MIT to cancer research—shows how grit and a love of learning can break barriers.

articles.title: MIT's Gooey Solution: A Gel That Sticks Around to Deliver Drugs Right Where It Hurts
articles.summary: Treating esophageal diseases is tough because drugs zip through too fast. MIT engineers created a hydrogel laced with bile salts that temporarily loosens cell junctions, letting a drug like infliximab soak into tissue. In animal tests, it worked, and cells returned to normal within three days.
